why_math: Diffusion works because it breaks impossible-to-sample complexity into tiny steps, each from a learned local pattern, and reversing noise progressively forces the model toward high-probability regions where real meshes live.

Multiple staggered partitions span more of the solution space than single partitions alone because different cuts through a domain capture different low-frequency patterns; combining them gives bases that converge faster.
Dual guidance works because two independent control signals—semantic intent and structural template—can be fused via attention weights, letting the model honor both without sacrificing either.

The lookup table replaces sign detection because voxel connectivity patterns are finite; enumerating all local shapes and storing their face counts lets you mesh topologically-complex unsigned surfaces without needing sign changes.

SMPL acts as a universal pivot because it solves the correspondence bottleneck: rather than matching diverse clothes-to-body pairs directly, routing through one canonical skeleton reuses proven human-fitting geometry.

Parallel transport along path-space geometry preserves image-space structure because following the underlying surface curvature keeps lines coherent under light variation, mathematically anchored by how objects orient in 3D.

The spatial acceleration tree defines the planar map itself because hierarchy cells partition the plane into regions; curve-curve collisions automatically induce topology, and numerical errors stay inside cell boundaries.

Soft maxed Voronoi regions preserve gradients because smooth blending of nearest-site contributions lets backprop flow through all contributing sites, enabling jointly optimal site placement and appearance.

Optimal transport (power diagrams) balances load and communication because it moves mass to equalize density across partitions; the resulting boundaries naturally minimize data crossing domain splits.
Releasing new LED rows as area grows preserves density because the rate of new rows per revolution equals the rate the troposkein expands, keeping pixels-per-unit-area constant by design.

Sampling opaque points from Gaussians works because each point is independently weighted by its Gaussian's strength; averaging many random samples converges to the true blended opacity by the law of large numbers.

The closed-form convolution works because a Gaussian blurred by another Gaussian (the circle of confusion) is still a Gaussian; the error function solution computes this composite shape exactly and differentiably.

Joint sampling-integration learns because paired networks can specialize: the sampler places points where the integrator needs them most, and training on integrands reveals which features matter, unlike blind averaging.
Branch-and-bound prunes by maintaining gap bounds: each subdivision tightens the true distance's range; once the gap narrows below tolerance, you have a certified answer without exhaustive search.

Vertex colors bypass UV problems because color at a vertex applies directly to its local geometry; converting textures to colors once front-loads the correspondence cost, then all downstream tools inherit texture awareness.
